metaDescription: Bissell cordless stick vacuums compared by motor wattage, brushroll design, removable battery and weight, so you match the right model to your floors and pets.
expertTake: The Bissell PowerClean DualBrush 4196K is the most capable stick in the family, and the PowerClean 200W 4173 is the value pick for a mixed-floor home. The Featherweight 3061 is the one to buy if lifting the machine is your main worry. Skip the category if you need a vacuum for a large carpeted house on one charge; a corded upright does that job better.
introParagraphs: One maker can sell cordless sticks across a wide spread of motors, brushrolls and batteries, and the model names change often. That makes it easy to buy a model that is lighter or weaker than the one you meant to get, especially when two listings look almost identical in photos.

The useful way to sort them is by what each one is built to do: pet hair, bare floors, light daily pickups or heavier mixed cleaning. Battery type, whether it clicks out, and the weight in your hand matter as much as any suction figure.

products.name: Bissell PowerClean DualBrush 280W 4196K cordless
products.description:
Two brushes share one head here. One loosens embedded dirt and hair, while the second hugs the floor to collect what the first lifts, including fine debris that a single roller tends to flick past. The head adapts to the surface so you are not changing settings between a rug and a tile hallway.

It sits above the PowerClean FurGuard 4039 because of that second brush; both use a 280W motor and list up to 50 minutes in low mode, so the head is the real difference. You pay for it in a slightly larger head and more brush parts to keep clear. The removable battery means a second pack can double your working time, and because makers rate each pack at its lowest setting, this 50 minute figure and the identical claim on the FurGuard 4039 say little about how fast the pack drains once you use carpet or boost. Compare the head and motor, not the minute count.

In practice this means a mixed home does not need a separate setting for the kitchen tile and the living room rug, which is the habit that most often gets skipped with a cordless stick. Check both brushes for hair after a pet-heavy session, since two rollers give hair two places to wrap. Wash the dust cup and filter on the manual's schedule, let them dry fully, and store it on its own stand or the wall mount so the head is not resting on the floor.
products.bestFor: Homes with mixed rugs and hard floors that want the most capable Bissell stick.
pros: Dual brushes pick up coarse and fine debris
cons: Two brushes mean more hair to clear
Head is larger than the Featherweight's

products.name: Bissell PowerClean FurGuard 280W 4039 self-cleaning
products.description:
FurGuard is the answer to the chore that ruins cordless vacuums for pet owners: cutting hair off the roller. The brush cleans itself as it runs, and the kit adds specialized tools for couches and stairs where fur collects.

Between this and the 200W FurFinder 4052, the 280W motor is the main upgrade, and it matters on a long-haired cat or a dog that sheds heavily. It gives up the second brush of the DualBrush 4196K, which suits a household that cares more about hair than about fine dust on hard floors.

Empty the bin before it reaches the fill line so hair does not compact, and wash the filter monthly. The self-cleaning roller still benefits from a glance at its ends every few weeks, and the wall mount keeps the charging plug off the floor.
products.bestFor: Dog and cat homes that want the roller to clear itself.
cons: Single brush misses some fine hard-floor dust
Runtime figure is the low-mode number

products.name: Bissell PowerClean 200W 4173 self-standing stick
products.description:
The 4173 is the plain PowerClean: a 200W motor, a tangle-free roller and a wall mount, with none of the specialised tools. That focus is exactly why it is a good everyday machine for an apartment or a house with mostly hard floors.

Against the FurFinder 4052, which shares the 200W motor, you give up the dedicated pet attachment. Against the 280W models you give up about ten minutes of rated runtime and some deep-carpet pull. If you need a stick that lives on a wall and handles daily crumbs, that gap rarely matters.

Rinse the dust cup, tap out the filter, and check the roller each month. Because the battery is the wear item, note that it is worth confirming the replacement pack is listed for sale before it fades.
products.bestFor: Everyday cleaning on mostly hard floors with light carpet.
pros: Low entry point in the PowerClean line
Stands alone or hangs on the wall

products.name: Bissell PowerClean FurFinder 200W 4052 cordless
products.description:
FurFinder is about seeing the hair. Bright headlights show fur that disappears into carpet and under furniture, and the matching FurFinder tool is meant for the couch and stairs. The removable battery is a real point in its favor at this level.

The same 200W motor as the plain 4173 gives it nothing extra for suction, so the extra money buys visibility and the pet attachment. If you already own a good handheld for upholstery, the 4173 does more for less.

Wipe the headlight lens, rinse the cup and filter, and keep the second battery charged if you buy one. Check the roller ends for hair as with any stick.
products.bestFor: Pet owners who want to see what they are missing under furniture.
cons: No suction gain over the plain 4173
Runtime still limited to about 40 minutes
Costs more than a bare 200W stick

products.name: Bissell CleanView XR Pet 300W cordless 3797V
products.description:
This is the strongest motor on the list at 300W, paired with a 24V removable battery. The FurBrush is aimed at embedded pet hair in carpet. On the spec sheet it out-muscles the 280W PowerClean sticks, though a bigger motor is not always better airflow.

It belongs to the older CleanView XR family, so the design is less polished than the newer PowerClean models: no wall-mount focus, less fine tuning. Compared with the CleanView XR 3789U, which uses a 200W motor and lists 35 minutes, it is the one to pick for fur, and it also carries a larger tank than the lighter Featherweight models so you stop to empty it less often during a long session on a shedding dog's favorite rug.

Keep the battery off the charger once full when you can, and empty the tank before it is packed. Replace the filter on schedule; a clogged filter makes a strong motor sound loud and clean poorly. One practical note on the family: this CleanView XR line and the newer PowerClean line are different generations, so accessories and batteries are not interchangeable. Buy any spare pack by the exact model number printed on the stick, not by the series name, or you will end up with a battery that does not fit.
products.bestFor: Pet households who want the biggest motor in the Bissell cordless group.
pros: Largest motor of the group at 300W
cons: Older design than the PowerClean line
Runtime is modest at this power

products.name: Bissell Featherweight 3061 cordless stick, self-standing
products.description:
The Featherweight earns its name: it is built for grab-and-go quick pickups rather than whole-house deep cleaning. The handle folds in two directions for tight storage, and it converts to a high-reach or handheld tool.

Compared with the 280W PowerClean sticks it is far weaker on carpet, so look at it as a light daily sweeper. For someone who finds a heavier stick tiring, the lighter weight matters more than the missing suction.

Keep the filter clean, empty the small cup often, and note the battery is the wear item. If lifting is your concern, this is the easiest model to carry upstairs.
products.bestFor: Quick daily pickups and anyone who struggles with heavier sticks, with the caveat that its small cup and modest battery make it a supplement to a stronger machine in a large home rather than a replacement for one.
pros: Very light for carrying and stairs

buyingCriteria.explanation: The PowerClean 4173 and FurFinder 4052 list 200W, the FurGuard 4039 and DualBrush 4196K list 280W, and the CleanView XR Pet 3797V lists 300W. Wattage is the electrical input, not the pull at the floor, so airflow and the head design decide what reaches the carpet. Use it to rank within the Bissell family rather than against other brands.

The 4196K, 4052 and 3797V use clickable packs, which lets you keep a spare charged and replace a worn pack without buying a new vacuum. Lithium-ion packs fade in roughly two to five years, so a removable one extends the machine's life. Confirm Bissell sells the specific pack before you rely on it.

A tangle-free roller on the 4173 suits light shedding, the 4039 self-cleans for heavy fur, and the 4196K uses two brushes for fine debris. Pick the brush to match the mess: a single roller on a hard floor pushes fine dust, while two collect it. Hair wrap is the top year-three complaint on any stick.

The 4039 and 4196K list up to 50 minutes and the 4173 and 4052 list 40, but those are low-mode figures. Turbo drains a pack in a fraction of that. Plan on about 25 minutes of realistic cleaning from a 40 minute rated pack, and buy a second battery if your home is large.

The Featherweight 3061 is the light end of this lineup and the 300W 3797V the heavier. A heavier stick tires your wrist on stairs and ceilings, so match weight to who uses it. Self-standing models like the 4173 save you leaning the stick against furniture.

The FurFinder 4052 and FurGuard 4039 include pet-focused tools, while the 4173 leaves them out. If you vacuum couches and stairs, the tool matters as much as the floor head. Count tools in the box, because a stick without them leaves you buying a handheld. The corded and handheld-only Bissell models that appear in the same search results are a different purchase, so check that the listing says cordless stick before you order.

specDecoder.meaning: Electrical power drawn by the motor, not a measure of suction. Two machines at the same wattage can clean very differently.
specDecoder.watchFor: Compare the 200W 4173 with the 280W 4039 inside the Bissell family only.

specDecoder.meaning: Higher voltage can deliver more power for the same current. It does not tell you capacity or runtime.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 3797V lists a 24V pack; the Featherweight uses a smaller battery for weight.

specDecoder.meaning: Runtime at the lowest power setting. Boost and carpet use cut it sharply.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 50 minute claim on the 4196K is a low-mode number.

specDecoder.meaning: The stick stays upright on its own without leaning, thanks to a balanced base or stand.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 4173 and 4052 stand alone, and a wall mount adds a safer parking spot. A stick that leans against a wall tends to slide, so a self-standing base is worth real money.

specDecoder.meaning: A roller shaped to push hair toward the bin rather than winding it around the shaft.
specDecoder.watchFor: No design is immune; check the roller ends on the 3797V monthly.

howWeEvaluated.title: Spec-sheet comparison within the brand
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared motor wattage, battery type and listed runtime across the Bissell cordless models. The 3797V at 300W topped the motor list, while the 4173 and 4052 sat at 200W.

howWeEvaluated.title: Head and brush design
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each head handles hair and fine debris. The 4196K two-brush design and the 4039 self-cleaning roller target different problems.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery serviceability
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored models with removable batteries, since a click-out pack makes a spare or replacement possible. Models without it were marked down for long-term ownership.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed carrying effort, folding handles and wall mounts. The Featherweight 3061 leads for light handling, and the PowerClean models for storage.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for recurring owner themes such as hair wrap, runtime shortfalls and battery wear. These shaped the cons rather than any single complaint.

Adds lights and a pet tool

cards.label: Removable battery
cards.text: The 4196K, 4052 and 3797V let you swap a pack. A spare doubles working time and a worn pack can be replaced instead of the whole machine.

cards.label: Built-in battery
cards.text: Models like the Featherweight 3061 charge in place. They are lighter and simpler, but when the cells fade you are stuck unless the battery is serviceable.

howToChoose.note: Large homes and long-term owners should pick removable.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A model that stands or hangs on a wall, converts to handheld, and stores in a small space. Weight matters because apartments often mean stairs.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Featherweight 3061 folds smallest and weighs least. The PowerClean 4173 has a wall mount and enough power for a mixed-floor flat.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have pets or thick carpet. The 4196K, 4039 or 3797V give more motor and better brush design, and a removable battery pays back over several years.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have mostly hard floors and light use. The 4173 or Featherweight 3061 cover quick daily cleaning at a lower tier.

maintenance.why: Hair wraps the ends and slows the motor. The 4196K has two rollers, so check both.
A clogged filter cuts airflow and shortens battery runtime. Dry fully before refitting.

maintenance.interval: After each use for the small cups
maintenance.why: A full cup reduces suction. The Featherweight cup is small and fills quickly.
Packs sitting empty age faster. Keep a spare on a partial charge.

Dust on the contacts causes intermittent charging. Match any replacement filter or battery to the exact model number on the stick, because the PowerClean, CleanView XR and Featherweight lines use different parts.

faq.q: Which Bissell cordless is best for pet hair?
faq.a: The PowerClean FurGuard 4039 has a self-cleaning roller and a 280W motor, which suits heavy shedders. The CleanView XR Pet 3797V has the largest motor in the group.

faq.q: Do the 200W and 280W models differ much?
faq.a: Yes, in deep carpet and on stubborn debris, and in rated runtime. For hard floors the 200W 4173 is often enough.

faq.q: Can I buy a spare battery?
faq.a: Models like the 4196K and 3797V use removable packs, so a spare is practical. Confirm the exact pack is sold for your model before relying on it.

faq.q: Is the Featherweight strong enough for carpet?
faq.a: It handles light carpet and rugs, but not thick pile. Use it for quick pickups and hard floors.

faq.q: How long should a Bissell cordless last?
faq.a: The motor and body can last years; the battery is the limit, typically fading in two to five years. A removable pack makes that repair easy.

faq.q: Are the corded Bissell sticks a better value?
faq.a: Corded models have no battery to wear out, but they tie you to an outlet. This guide covers cordless only.
